bull_bear.body:
- In-house Research & Development Centre: 108 new products were developed during the year, both for new market segments and to enhance existing lines in domestic and export markets.
- Import substitution / share gain from multinationals: the Company used the demand slowdown to introduce and get approved new products in place of existing multinational competitors, strengthening long-term positioning.
- Technology absorption in process automation, heavy duty cam follower manufacturing and processing of heavy duty bearing races, plus design and development of needle bush and thrust bearings.
- Technology-partner associates: 35% held NRB-IBC Bearings Private Limited (joint venture with IBC Industrial Bearings and Components AG, Switzerland) and 35% held NIBL-Korta Engineering Private Limited (formerly part of Korta group, Spain), both of which grew turnover and added new customers in FY2025-26.
- Customised, non-standard product capability targeted at specific OEM sectors (Material Handling, Agriculture, Industrial Electrical, Industrial Transmission).
- Cost discipline: stringent cost control measures, particularly in managing raw material and finished goods inventory, resulting in improved cost efficiency.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Import competition from Chinese machines and mechanical components, including bearings — Management states the rapid growth of imports of Chinese machines and mechanical components including bearings is reshaping the market, and that rising adoption of imported Chinese harvester machines eroded market share for local manufacturers, impacting revenue from the agriculture segment.
- Automotive bearing manufacturers pivoting into the industrial segment — Complemented by the Government's initiative to promote the Electric Vehicle segment, several automotive bearing manufacturers began redirecting their focus toward the industrial sector, resulting in intensified competition and a more saturated market landscape - directly in NIBL's core industrial-bearing market.
- Customer / OEM schedule concentration in weak end-segments — A significant decline in schedules from key OEMs in the textile and Radial Piston Pump segments, along with reduced demand from textile end-users, affected revenue in those segments - showing dependence on a small set of OEM schedules.
- End-market cyclicality and uneven segment performance — While Industrial Gearboxes, Construction Machinery, Material Handling Equipment and Machine Tools performed in line with forecasts, Textile Machinery and Mining fell short of expectations; management notes market dynamics remain volatile and demand patterns continue to evolve.
- Global macro and geopolitical exposure — The overall business environment remained challenging within the industrial segment due to global economic uncertainty, rising geopolitical tensions, and disruptions caused by inter-country conflicts and policy shifts.
- Foreign-exchange and export-market exposure — The Company reports foreign exchange earnings of Rs. 2,300.31 lakhs and outgo of Rs. 586.79 lakhs for FY2025-26, and its growth mantra rests on entering new export markets such as the USA and South East Asian countries, so a material share of business is exposed to currency and cross-border trade conditions.
- Input-cost and energy-cost exposure — Cost efficiency in the year came from stringent cost control in raw material and finished goods inventory; the energy annexure shows propane gas cost rose to Rs. 1,78,400 per ton from Rs. 69,800, and solar generation fell to 1,31,473 KWh from 3,19,879 KWh, leaving more of the load on purchased power.
- Reduced statutory corporate-governance perimeter — Based on paid-up equity share capital and net worth, the corporate governance provisions of SEBI LODR are not applicable to the Company; it provides a Corporate Governance report only on a voluntary basis. CSR provisions of Section 135 are likewise not applicable, and no CSR policy or activities exist.

business.body: The Company manufactures bearings for industrial applications, and states there has been no change in the main nature of its business during FY2025-26. It runs a manufacturing facility supported by a fully equipped Research & Development Centre that develops new products aligned to evolving customer requirements and enhances existing product lines. NIBL sells to domestic OEMs and distribution channels and exports, and holds 35% stakes in two associate companies, NRB-IBC Bearings Private Limited and NIBL-Korta Engineering Private Limited.

outlook.body:
- Target specific OEM sectors - Material Handling, Agriculture, Industrial Electrical and Industrial Transmission - offering customized bearing solutions for each.
- Develop customer-centric, non-standard products as the stated strategic priority for FY2025-26.
- Strengthen the distribution footprint in untapped markets, particularly Tier 2 cities across India, to reach emerging industrial clusters.
- Expand presence in underpenetrated regions of India, Asia and the Americas; in exports, new product development and entry into new markets such as the USA and South East Asian countries.
- Continue investing in the manufacturing facility and the fully equipped R&D Centre, both for new product development aligned to customer requirements and for enhancing existing product lines to meet rising performance benchmarks.
- Substitute multinational competitors' products: the Company used the demand slowdown to introduce and get new products approved in place of existing multinational competitors, strengthening long-term positioning.
- Maintain stringent cost control, particularly in managing raw material and finished goods inventory, for improved cost efficiency.
- Extend the R&D product range across needle bush bearings, CN type needle bush, needle roller and roller thrust bearings, cylindrical roller bearings, precision rollers and races.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report describes no named plant, line or capacity project with a commissioning or ramp timeline. Expansion is framed qualitatively: the Company states it continues to invest in its manufacturing facility, supported by a fully equipped Research & Development Centre whose team works on new product development aligned with evolving customer requirements and on enhancing existing product lines. In line with its expansion strategy NIBL is strengthening its distribution footprint in untapped markets, particularly Tier 2 cities across India, to reach emerging industrial clusters, and is expanding its presence in underpenetrated regions of India, Asia and the Americas, with new export markets such as the USA and South East Asian countries. A capital-commitments note is disclosed (estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account and not provided for, net of advances of Rs. 200.28 lakhs; as at March 31, 2025: Rs. 37.22 lakhs), but the block supplied does not allow the commitment figure itself to be attributed to a period.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The global bearing market is valued at approximately $156.2 billion and is projected to grow at a CAGR of 9.8% to over $301 billion by 2033, propelled by rapid industrial automation, the electric vehicle (EV) transition, and modernization of aerospace and railway sectors.
- India's real GDP grew by a resilient 7.7% in Financial Year 2026, driven by robust domestic demand, strong services exports and private investment; the domestic political scenario remained stable.
- The overall business environment remained challenging within the industrial segment due to global economic uncertainty, rising geopolitical tensions, and disruptions caused by inter-country conflicts and policy shifts.
- Rapid growth of imports of Chinese machines and mechanical components including bearings, complemented by the Government's initiative to promote the Electric Vehicle segment, led several automotive bearing manufacturers to redirect focus toward the industrial sector, intensifying competition and saturating the market.
- Industrial Gearboxes, Construction Machinery, Material Handling Equipment and Machine Tools performed in line with forecasts, while Textile Machinery and Mining fell short of expectations.
- Rising adoption of imported Chinese harvester machines eroded market share for local manufacturers, impacting revenue from the agriculture segment.
- A significant decline in schedules from key OEMs in the textile and Radial Piston Pump segments, along with reduced demand from textile end-users, affected revenue in those segments.
- Successful penetration of the domestic market in both the distribution and OEM segments.
- Market dynamics remain volatile and demand patterns continue to evolve; management states NIBL remains agile, evaluating changing trends and realigning its business strategy to ensure continued growth and market relevance.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body: - **Industrial bearings:** Needle bush bearings, Needle roller and roller thrust bearings, Cylindrical roller bearings, Cam followers (including heavy series cam follower), Thrust washers (special heavy series), Races (including races for heavy duty ball bearing series), Combined radial and axial bearings, Spherical roller bearings in 213 series, Precision rollers

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Industrial Gearboxes

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The global bearing market is valued at approximately $156.2 billion and is projected to grow at a CAGR of 9.8% to over $301 billion by 2033, propelled by rapid industrial automation, the electric vehicle (EV) transition, and modernization of aerospace and railway sectors.
- India's real GDP grew by a resilient 7.7% in Financial Year 2026, driven by robust domestic demand, strong services exports and private investment; the domestic political scenario remained stable.
- The overall business environment remained challenging within the industrial segment due to global economic uncertainty, rising geopolitical tensions, and disruptions caused by inter-country conflicts and policy shifts.
- Rapid growth of imports of Chinese machines and mechanical components including bearings, complemented by the Government's initiative to promote the Electric Vehicle segment, led several automotive bearing manufacturers to redirect focus toward the industrial sector, intensifying competition and saturating the market.
- Industrial Gearboxes, Construction Machinery, Material Handling Equipment and Machine Tools performed in line with forecasts, while Textile Machinery and Mining fell short of expectations.
- Rising adoption of imported Chinese harvester machines eroded market share for local manufacturers, impacting revenue from the agriculture segment.
- A significant decline in schedules from key OEMs in the textile and Radial Piston Pump segments, along with reduced demand from textile end-users, affected revenue in those segments.
- Successful penetration of the domestic market in both the distribution and OEM segments.
- Market dynamics remain volatile and demand patterns continue to evolve; management states NIBL remains agile, evaluating changing trends and realigning its business strategy to ensure continued growth and market relevance.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Target specific OEM sectors - Material Handling, Agriculture, Industrial Electrical and Industrial Transmission - offering customized bearing solutions for each.
- Develop customer-centric, non-standard products as the stated strategic priority for FY2025-26.
- Strengthen the distribution footprint in untapped markets, particularly Tier 2 cities across India, to reach emerging industrial clusters.
- Expand presence in underpenetrated regions of India, Asia and the Americas; in exports, new product development and entry into new markets such as the USA and South East Asian countries.
- Continue investing in the manufacturing facility and the fully equipped R&D Centre, both for new product development aligned to customer requirements and for enhancing existing product lines to meet rising performance benchmarks.
- Substitute multinational competitors' products: the Company used the demand slowdown to introduce and get new products approved in place of existing multinational competitors, strengthening long-term positioning.
- Maintain stringent cost control, particularly in managing raw material and finished goods inventory, for improved cost efficiency.
- Extend the R&D product range across needle bush bearings, CN type needle bush, needle roller and roller thrust bearings, cylindrical roller bearings, precision rollers and races.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report describes no named plant, line or capacity project with a commissioning or ramp timeline. Expansion is framed qualitatively: the Company states it continues to invest in its manufacturing facility, supported by a fully equipped Research & Development Centre whose team works on new product development aligned with evolving customer requirements and on enhancing existing product lines. In line with its expansion strategy NIBL is strengthening its distribution footprint in untapped markets, particularly Tier 2 cities across India, to reach emerging industrial clusters, and is expanding its presence in underpenetrated regions of India, Asia and the Americas, with new export markets such as the USA and South East Asian countries. A capital-commitments note is disclosed (estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account and not provided for, net of advances of Rs. 200.28 lakhs; as at March 31, 2025: Rs. 37.22 lakhs), but the block supplied does not allow the commitment figure itself to be attributed to a period.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- In-house Research & Development Centre: 108 new products were developed during the year, both for new market segments and to enhance existing lines in domestic and export markets.
- Import substitution / share gain from multinationals: the Company used the demand slowdown to introduce and get approved new products in place of existing multinational competitors, strengthening long-term positioning.
- Technology absorption in process automation, heavy duty cam follower manufacturing and processing of heavy duty bearing races, plus design and development of needle bush and thrust bearings.
- Technology-partner associates: 35% held NRB-IBC Bearings Private Limited (joint venture with IBC Industrial Bearings and Components AG, Switzerland) and 35% held NIBL-Korta Engineering Private Limited (formerly part of Korta group, Spain), both of which grew turnover and added new customers in FY2025-26.
- Customised, non-standard product capability targeted at specific OEM sectors (Material Handling, Agriculture, Industrial Electrical, Industrial Transmission).
- Cost discipline: stringent cost control measures, particularly in managing raw material and finished goods inventory, resulting in improved cost efficiency.

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Import competition from Chinese machines and mechanical components, including bearings — Management states the rapid growth of imports of Chinese machines and mechanical components including bearings is reshaping the market, and that rising adoption of imported Chinese harvester machines eroded market share for local manufacturers, impacting revenue from the agriculture segment.
- Automotive bearing manufacturers pivoting into the industrial segment — Complemented by the Government's initiative to promote the Electric Vehicle segment, several automotive bearing manufacturers began redirecting their focus toward the industrial sector, resulting in intensified competition and a more saturated market landscape - directly in NIBL's core industrial-bearing market.
- Customer / OEM schedule concentration in weak end-segments — A significant decline in schedules from key OEMs in the textile and Radial Piston Pump segments, along with reduced demand from textile end-users, affected revenue in those segments - showing dependence on a small set of OEM schedules.
- End-market cyclicality and uneven segment performance — While Industrial Gearboxes, Construction Machinery, Material Handling Equipment and Machine Tools performed in line with forecasts, Textile Machinery and Mining fell short of expectations; management notes market dynamics remain volatile and demand patterns continue to evolve.
- Global macro and geopolitical exposure — The overall business environment remained challenging within the industrial segment due to global economic uncertainty, rising geopolitical tensions, and disruptions caused by inter-country conflicts and policy shifts.
- Foreign-exchange and export-market exposure — The Company reports foreign exchange earnings of Rs. 2,300.31 lakhs and outgo of Rs. 586.79 lakhs for FY2025-26, and its growth mantra rests on entering new export markets such as the USA and South East Asian countries, so a material share of business is exposed to currency and cross-border trade conditions.
- Input-cost and energy-cost exposure — Cost efficiency in the year came from stringent cost control in raw material and finished goods inventory; the energy annexure shows propane gas cost rose to Rs. 1,78,400 per ton from Rs. 69,800, and solar generation fell to 1,31,473 KWh from 3,19,879 KWh, leaving more of the load on purchased power.
- Reduced statutory corporate-governance perimeter — Based on paid-up equity share capital and net worth, the corporate governance provisions of SEBI LODR are not applicable to the Company; it provides a Corporate Governance report only on a voluntary basis. CSR provisions of Section 135 are likewise not applicable, and no CSR policy or activities exist.
